top_stories.title: Judge sides with Anthropic to temporarily block the Pentagon's ban
top_stories.summary: A federal judge has temporarily blocked the Pentagon's designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk, siding with the AI company's request for an injunction. The ruling halts the ban while the legal challenge proceeds, a significant development for the growing relationship between AI firms and the US defence establishment. Anthropic had argued the designation was unfair and damaging to its business.

top_stories.title: A leak reveals that Anthropic is testing a more capable AI model "Claude Mythos"
top_stories.summary: A data leak has revealed that Anthropic is internally testing a new AI model called Claude Mythos, described as representing a "step change in capabilities" over existing Claude models. The existence of the model was not previously publicly known. Fortune reports Anthropic has confirmed it is testing the model following the leak.

top_stories.title: Google's 'live' AI search assistant can handle conversations in dozens more languages
top_stories.summary: Google has expanded its 'live' AI search assistant to support conversations in dozens more languages, significantly broadening its reach beyond English-speaking users. The feature allows users to hold real-time spoken conversations with Google's AI search product. The expansion is part of Google's broader push to make its AI tools globally accessible.

top_stories.title: Wikipedia bans AI-generated articles
top_stories.summary: Wikipedia has introduced a ban on AI-generated articles, citing concerns about accuracy, sourcing, and the integrity of the encyclopaedia's editorial standards. The policy reflects growing tension between AI-generated content and the norms of academic and reference publishing. Editors will be expected to flag and remove content identified as AI-generated.

top_stories.title: STADLER reshapes knowledge work at a 230-year-old company
top_stories.summary: OpenAI's official blog profiles how STADLER, a rail vehicle manufacturer with over 230 years of history, has deployed AI tools to transform knowledge work across its organisation. The case study details how employees are using AI to streamline documentation, engineering queries, and internal processes. It is part of OpenAI's ongoing series showcasing enterprise AI adoption.

further_links.title: David Sacks is no longer the White House AI and Crypto Czar
further_links.summary: David Sacks has stepped down from his role as the White House's AI and Crypto Czar, marking a significant shift in the administration's AI policy leadership.

further_links.title: Google is making it easier to import another AI's memory into Gemini
further_links.summary: Google is introducing a feature that allows users to import conversation history and memory from other AI assistants directly into Gemini, lowering the barrier to switching platforms.

further_links.title: Apple will reportedly allow other AI chatbots to plug into Siri
further_links.summary: Apple is reportedly planning to open Siri to third-party AI chatbot integrations as part of an update coming in iOS 27, broadening the assistant's capabilities.

further_links.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash Live: Making audio AI more natural and reliable
further_links.summary: Google DeepMind has announced Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, a new model update aimed at making real-time audio AI interactions more natural, low-latency, and reliable.

further_links.title: New York City hospitals drop Palantir as controversial AI firm expands in UK
further_links.summary: New York City hospitals have ended their contract with Palantir just as the controversial AI and data analytics firm is expanding its footprint in the UK health sector.

further_links.title: AI Research Is Getting Harder to Separate From Geopolitics
further_links.summary: Wired reports that AI research produced in China is increasingly diverging from Western output along geopolitical lines, with collaboration and citation patterns reflecting growing tensions.

further_links.title: Webtoon is adding AI localization tools to its comics platform
further_links.summary: Webtoon is integrating AI-powered translation and localization tools into its Canvas platform to help creators reach global audiences more easily.

further_links.title: I Asked ChatGPT 500 Questions. Here Are the Ads I Saw Most Often
further_links.summary: Wired's investigation into ChatGPT's advertising patterns reveals which brands and sectors appear most frequently in responses across hundreds of queries.

further_links.title: EU backs nude app ban and delays to landmark AI rules
further_links.summary: The EU has backed a ban on AI-powered nudification apps while also agreeing to delay implementation of certain provisions of its landmark AI Act.

further_links.title: AI users whose lives were wrecked by delusion
further_links.summary: The Guardian reports on cases where heavy reliance on AI chatbots led to serious real-world harm, as users formed unhealthy attachments or trusted AI outputs uncritically.

ethan_mollick.title: Why are executives enamored with AI, but ICs aren't?
ethan_mollick.summary: This post from johnjwang.com — surfaced in today's feed — explores the divergence in AI enthusiasm between senior executives and individual contributors, arguing that the gap reflects differences in how each group experiences AI's benefits and risks in their daily work. Executives tend to see AI as a strategic lever, while ICs are more likely to encounter its limitations hands-on. The piece draws on observations about workplace adoption patterns to explain why top-down AI mandates often fall flat.

email_teaser: Anthropic has a new secret model and a courtroom win against the Pentagon — two big stories shaping the AI landscape today. Plus: Wikipedia bans AI-generated articles, Google expands its live AI assistant to dozens more languages, and OpenAI profiles a 230-year-old company going all-in on AI.
